39.title: Sequence gaps: where did invoice 1003 go? 🔢 #sql #oracle #shorts
39.yt:
39. Invoice 1002 → then 1005 😳
Where did 1003 and 1004 go? 🕵️
Gaps are NOT a bug 💡

🔢 Sequence = a number dispenser, no table lock
🧠 CACHE 20 → 20 numbers in memory, 1 dictionary write per 20
↩️ NEXTVAL is never rolled back
🕳️ 3 sources of gaps:
   → ROLLBACK: the number is used, the row is gone
   → instance restart: cached numbers are lost
   → RAC: one cache per node → unique, not in time order
☠️ SELECT MAX(id) + 1 → two sessions, same id → ORA-00001
🆔 12c+: GENERATED ALWAYS / BY DEFAULT / BY DEFAULT ON NULL AS IDENTITY
   → still a sequence underneath, same gaps
🐢 NOCACHE + busy inserts → "enq: SQ - contention"
   → ALTER SEQUENCE … CACHE 1000
⏱️ Need time order? Store a timestamp, not the id
🧾 Truly gap-free? Counter row + FOR UPDATE in the same transaction
   → price: inserts wait for each other

Sequences promise UNIQUE numbers, not gap-free ones 💡

Have you ever been asked to "fix the gaps"? 👇

40.title: ROWNUM trap: your top-10 query returns the wrong rows 🔟 #sql #oracle #shorts
40.yt:
40. "Top 10 biggest payments"
WHERE ROWNUM ≤ 10 ORDER BY amount DESC
Fast. Looks right. WRONG rows 😱

🔢 ROWNUM is assigned BEFORE ORDER BY
   → Oracle takes the first 10 it finds, then sorts them
🚫 WHERE ROWNUM greater than 1 → always 0 rows
   → the next row becomes #1 again… forever
✅ Pre-12c: sort in an inline view, ROWNUM outside
   → plan: SORT ORDER BY STOPKEY
✨ 12c+: ORDER BY … FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY
   → OFFSET 20 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY
   → WITH TIES: keeps rows equal to the last one
🐌 Page 10,000 with OFFSET = read 100,000 rows, keep 10
⚡ Keyset pagination: continue after the last row
   → rows with an earlier created, or same created and a smaller id
   → index (created, id) → every page equally fast
🔁 Same row on 2 pages? End ORDER BY with a unique column

Sort first, cut second, continue from the last row 💡

Do your screens still use OFFSET for deep pages? 👇

41.title: ORA-04091 mutating table: the right fix 💥 #sql #oracle #shorts
41.yt:
41. One UPDATE. One trigger.
ORA-04091: table is mutating, trigger may not see it 💥
Why does Oracle stop you? 🤔

🔄 A ROW trigger fires while the UPDATE is still running
   → half the rows new, half old
   → a SUM read now is neither answer
⚠️ Happens when a row trigger reads/changes its OWN table
   → multi-row UPDATE / DELETE / INSERT … SELECT
   → single-row INSERT … VALUES and statement triggers are fine
🚫 "Fix" from the internet: PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION
   → sees only committed data → no error, WRONG result
✅ 11g+: COMPOUND TRIGGER
   → AFTER EACH ROW: just remember the ids
   → AFTER STATEMENT: table is complete → check safely
🧭 Better: business rules in the API package, CHECK constraints for simple rules
🧪 Always test triggers with a MULTI-row update

Remember rows in each row, do the work after the statement 💡

Have you hit ORA-04091 in production? 👇

42.title: PL/SQL collections: associative array vs nested table vs VARRAY 🧺 #sql #oracle #shorts
42.yt:
42. 3 kinds of arrays in PL/SQL 🧺
Pick the wrong one → ORA-06531 before you store a single value 😵

🗺️ ASSOCIATIVE ARRAY (INDEX BY)
   → key → value, even INDEX BY VARCHAR2(3) for 'USD'
   → no constructor, no EXTEND, gaps are fine
   → perfect in-memory lookup cache
📦 NESTED TABLE
   → no init → ORA-06531 · no EXTEND → ORA-06533
   → as a SQL type: SELECT … FROM TABLE(:ids)
📏 VARRAY(n)
   → fixed maximum, always dense, order kept
   → element n+1 → ORA-06532
🕳️ Trap: DELETE(3) then FOR i IN 1 .. COUNT → NO_DATA_FOUND
   → walk with FIRST / NEXT, or FORALL … INDICES OF
🎯 500 ids as ONE bind instead of 500 literals
🧰 COUNT · FIRST · LAST · NEXT · EXTEND · TRIM · DELETE · EXISTS (never raises)

Map, set or short list: pick the collection by its job 💡

Which one do you use the most? 👇

43.title: Oracle temporary tables: private rows for every session 🧊 #sql #oracle #shorts
43.yt:
43. 50 users run the same report 📊
All writing to ONE scratch table? 😬
Use temporary tables 🧊

🏗️ GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE: definition shared, rows PRIVATE per session
   → stored in TEMP, no locks between users
⏳ ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS (default) → empty after COMMIT
   ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS → kept until logout
   → TRUNCATE removes only YOUR rows
⚡ Less redo: rows need no recovery
   → 12c TEMP_UNDO_ENABLED → undo in TEMP, almost no redo
📈 10 rows here, 1M there → 12c session-private statistics
☠️ Trap: connection pools + PRESERVE ROWS → next user sees old rows
   → clean at the start of every call
🔒 18c PRIVATE TEMPORARY TABLES: even the definition is private
   → name must start with ORA$PTT_
✅ Create once in your install script, never inside procedures

One definition, private rows, always start clean 💡

Do you use GTTs or WITH clauses for scratch data? 👇

44.title: Pipelined table functions: SELECT from PL/SQL 🚰 #sql #oracle #shorts
44.yt:
44. SELECT * FROM my_plsql_function() 🤯
PL/SQL logic → rows you can JOIN and report on

📦 Normal table function: builds ALL rows in PGA, returns at the end
   → 1M rows = 1M rows in memory, caller waits
🚰 PIPELINED: PIPE ROW(r) streams each row immediately
   → first rows arrive at once, memory stays flat
🧱 Object type + table type + PIPELINED + PIPE ROW + RETURN;
   → SELECT * FROM TABLE(fees())  (12.2+: FROM fees())
🎯 Use cases:
   → parse CSV / CLOB into rows
   → one SELECT for the BI tool, rules stay in PL/SQL
   → streaming ETL: f3(f2(f1(source)))
🛑 FETCH FIRST 5 → NO_DATA_NEEDED inside the function → clean up, re-raise
🎲 Optimizer guesses 8168 rows → CARDINALITY hint / dynamic sampling
🚀 PARALLEL_ENABLE (PARTITION c BY ANY) → parallel servers

Stream rows from PL/SQL straight into SQL 💡
